concepts.name: Sovereignty in detail: dependency, dominion, Commonwealth and the UN

questions.q: India ceased to be a British dominion on 26 January 1950, according to Laxmikanth, by
o: withdrawing from the Commonwealth of Nations
the coming into force of the Indian Independence Act, 1947
a resolution of the United Nations accepting her as a sovereign State
questions.e: Footnote 2 (p.91): India ceased to be a British dominion on 26 January 1950 by declaring herself a sovereign republic. Footnote 3 and p.86: she stayed in the Commonwealth.
w: The chapter says India declared the continuation of her full Commonwealth membership in 1949; she did not withdraw.
The 1947 Act ended the dependency; the dominion status that followed lasted till 1950.
UN membership dates from 1945 and has no bearing on ending dominion status.

questions.q: In the words of Pandit Nehru quoted in the chapter, the very strength of the free association of the sovereign Commonwealth of Nations lies in
questions.a: its flexibility and its complete freedom
o: its flexibility and its complete freedom
the commitments it places on every member nation
the authority of the Crown over the member nations
the uniform laws that its member nations follow
questions.e: Footnote 3 (p.91): 'Its very strength lies in its flexibility and its complete freedom.'
w: Nehru said the free association does not involve the commitments which an alliance normally means.
The chapter says the acceptance of the Crown as head of the Commonwealth does not affect sovereignty; strength is not placed in its authority.
Nehru's remark says nothing of uniform laws; strength lies in flexibility and freedom.

questions.q: India became a member of the United Nations Organisation in 1945. According to the chapter, her political status at that time was that of
questions.a: a dependency (colony) of the British Empire
o: a dependency (colony) of the British Empire
a dominion in the British Commonwealth of Nations
a sovereign republic with her own Constitution
a dominion whose head of State was the President
questions.e: Footnote 4 (p.91): UN membership in 1945. Footnote 2 (p.91): India was a dependency till the Independence Act, 1947.
w: Dominion status began on 15 August 1947, after the UN date.
The republic came on 26 January 1950, five years after 1945.
There was no President before the republic of 1950; dominion status began in 1947 in any case.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's political status is NOT correct according to the chapter?
questions.a: India ceased to be a British dominion on 15 August 1947, the day of independence
o: India ceased to be a British dominion on 15 August 1947, the day of independence
Till the Indian Independence Act, 1947, India was a dependency (colony) of the British Empire
India ceased to be a British dominion on 26 January 1950 by declaring herself a sovereign republic
Pakistan continued to be a British Dominion until 1956
questions.e: Footnote 2 (p.91): from 15 August 1947 to 26 January 1950 India was a dominion; she ceased to be one on 26 January 1950. 15 August 1947 is when dominion status began.
w: This is stated in footnote 2: dependency status lasted until the 1947 Act, so it is a correct statement.
This is stated in footnote 2: the dominion status ended by a declaration on 26 January 1950, so it is correct.
This is stated in footnote 2: Pakistan stayed a dominion until 1956, so it is correct.

questions.q: The remarks of Pandit Nehru on the Commonwealth, quoted in the chapter, were made in 1949 in order to
questions.a: dispel the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly
o: dispel the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly
persuade the Constituent Assembly to take India out of the Commonwealth
obtain the consent of the Crown for India's continued membership
announce India's admission to the United Nations
questions.e: Footnote 3 (p.91): 'To dispel the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly, Pandit Nehru said in 1949 thus ...'.
w: Nehru said it is open to any member to go out, but he did not urge withdrawal; he allayed fears about the link.
Nothing in the chapter says the Crown's consent was needed; membership rests on free will.
UN membership dates from 1945 and is not the subject of the footnote.

questions.q:
With reference to Pandit Nehru's 1949 remarks on the Commonwealth, as quoted in the chapter, consider the following statements:

1. Nehru said that the pledge to achieve Purna Swaraj had been taken long ago and had been achieved.
2. Nehru said that an alliance normally means commitments, which the free association of the Commonwealth does not involve.
3. Nehru said that its strength lies in its flexibility and its complete freedom.
4. Nehru said that a member nation may go out of the Commonwealth only with the consent of the other members.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 3, p.91 records this. Statement 2 is correct: fn 3, p.91. Statement 3 is correct: fn 3, p.91. Statement 4 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: it is open to any member nation to go out if it so chooses.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the declaration India made in 1949:

1. In 1949 India declared the continuation of her full membership of the Commonwealth of Nations.
2. The declaration was made after India had ceased to be a dominion.
3. The declaration is an extra-constitutional one.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86 and fn 2, p.91: 1949 is earlier than 26 January 1950, when India ceased to be a dominion. Statement 3 is correct: p.86.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the dominion status of India and Pakistan:

1. India's dominion status ended in 1956, the year in which she declared herself a republic.
2. Pakistan continued to be a British Dominion until 1956.
3. India's political status from 15 August 1947 to 26 January 1950 was that of a dominion.
4. India's dominion status began in 1949 with the declaration on the Commonwealth.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 2, p.91: 26 January 1950; 1956 is the year Pakistan's dominion status ended. Statement 2 is correct: fn 2, p.91. Statement 3 is correct: fn 2, p.91. Statement 4 is incorrect: fn 2, p.91: it began on 15 August 1947.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the meaning of sovereignty in the chapter:

1. There is no authority above a sovereign State, which is free to conduct its own internal and external affairs.
2. India's freedom in her external affairs is subject to the consent of the Commonwealth.
3. The word 'sovereign' implies that India is neither a dependency nor a dominion of any other nation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86: the Commonwealth declaration does not affect her sovereignty in any manner. Statement 3 is correct: p.86.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.86
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. As a sovereign State India can acquire a foreign territory.
2. India's membership of the UNO in no way constitutes a limitation on her sovereignty.
3. India accepted the British Crown as the head of the Commonwealth.
4. The Commonwealth association is an agreement by free will, to be terminated by free will.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is correct: p.86. Statement 4 is correct: fn 3, p.91.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.86
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Pandit Nehru asked whether a nation loses its independence by an alliance with another country.
2. Pandit Nehru said that India had still to achieve Purna Swaraj.
3. Pandit Nehru spoke on the Commonwealth in 1950, after the Constitution came into force.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 3, p.91. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: he said 'We have achieved it'. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: he spoke in 1949.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. As a sovereign State, India has no authority above it.
2. India's external affairs need the prior approval of the Commonwealth, though her internal affairs are free.
3. India is free to conduct her internal affairs without outside authority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86: she is free to conduct both internal and external affairs. Statement 3 is correct: p.86.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.86
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the order of events:

1. India's membership of the UNO came before the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
2. India's declaration on the Commonwealth came before her membership of the UNO.
3. India's declaration on the Commonwealth came after she declared herself a sovereign republic.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 4 and fn 2, p.91: 1945 is earlier than 1947. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86 and fn 4: 1949 is later than 1945. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.86 and fn 2: 1949 is earlier than 26 January 1950.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 1949 remarks of Pandit Nehru:

1. They were made to reassure the British Parliament about India's loyalty to the Crown.
2. They were made to dispel the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly.
3. They are quoted in the chapter in support of the point that UN membership does not limit sovereignty.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: they were meant to dispel the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly. Statement 2 is correct: fn 3, p.91. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 3 is attached to the Commonwealth passage; fn 4 gives only the year of UN membership.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Till the passage of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, India was a dependency of the British Empire.
2. The 1949 Commonwealth declaration is a provision of the Constitution adopted in 1949.
3. It is open to any member nation to go out of the Commonwealth if it so chooses.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 2, p.91. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86: extra-constitutional. Statement 3 is correct: fn 3, p.91. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not none.
'Only one' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'All three' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not all three.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. India was a dominion of the British Commonwealth on the day her UN membership began.
2. In 1949 India accepted the British Crown as the head of the Commonwealth.
3. India's dominion status ended before Pakistan's did.
4. India declared herself a sovereign republic in 1947.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 4 and fn 2, p.91: in 1945 India was a dependency. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is correct: fn 2, p.91: January 1950 against Pakistan's 1956. Statement 4 is incorrect: fn 2, p.91: 26 January 1950. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' ignores statements 2 and 3, which are correct.
'Only one' misses one of the two correct statements (2 and 3).
'Only three' counts statement 1 or 4, which are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Pandit Nehru called the Commonwealth an agreement terminable only by the Crown.
2. Pandit Nehru said that a nation does lose its independence by an alliance with another country.
3. Pandit Nehru's remarks were aimed at the lurking fears of some members of the Constituent Assembly.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: terminated by free will. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 3, p.91: he asked, rhetorically, whether a nation loses independence by an alliance, and argued it does not. Statement 3 is correct: fn 3, p.91. So only one is correct.
w: 'None' ignores statement 3, which is correct.
'Only two' counts statement 1 or 2, which are incorrect.
'All three' counts statements 1 and 2, which are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: India ceased to be a British dominion on 26 January 1950.
Statement-II: India became a member of the UNO in 1945.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: fn 2, p.91. Statement-II is correct: fn 4, p.91. The two facts are independent; the date of UN membership gives no reason for the end of dominion status.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I, so 'does not explain' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Membership of the Commonwealth does not compromise India's sovereignty.
Statement-II: The free association of the sovereign Commonwealth of Nations does not involve the commitments that an alliance normally means.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.86 and fn 3. Statement-II is correct: fn 3, p.91. Nehru's answer to the fear that an association costs independence was exactly that it carries no such commitments.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I, so 'explains' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the period or year in List-I with the event in List-II.

List-I
A. 15 August 1947 to 26 January 1950
B. Till the Indian Independence Act, 1947
C. 1949
D. 1956

List-II
1. Pakistan ceases to be a British Dominion
2. India declares the continuation of her full Commonwealth membership
3. India is a dominion in the British Commonwealth of Nations
4. India is a dependency of the British Empire
questions.e: Footnote 2 and p.86 / fn 3 (pp.86, 91).
w: A and B are interchanged: dependency came first, then dominion.
C and D are interchanged: the declaration was 1949, Pakistan's dominion status ended 1956.
A and C are interchanged: the dominion period is 1947-50, the declaration 1949.

concepts.name: Socialism in detail: Avadi, democratic socialism and case law

questions.q: The Supreme Court's observation, cited in the chapter, that Indian socialism is a blend of Marxism and Gandhism, leaning heavily towards Gandhian socialism, comes from which case?
o: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2000)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
questions.e: p.86 with footnotes 7 and 8 (p.91): the Pant University case (2000) gives the aims of democratic socialism; the Nakara case (1982) gives the blend of Marxism and Gandhism.
w: The Pant University case is cited in the chapter for the aims of democratic socialism (end poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity).
Kesavananda Bharati is cited for the status and amendability of the Preamble, not for the nature of Indian socialism.
The Berubari reference is cited for the Preamble not being a part of the Constitution.

questions.q: According to the resolution of the Congress party at its Avadi session in 1955, planning should take place with a view to the establishment of
o: a society in which all means of production and distribution are nationalised
a mixed economy with the abolition of private property in land
a communistic pattern of society in which private property is abolished
questions.e: Footnote 5 (p.91): planning 'with a view to the establishment of a socialistic pattern of society'.
w: The resolution speaks of the principal means of production under social ownership or control, not nationalisation of all.
The chapter does not attribute land reform or the abolition of property in land to the resolution.
The chapter keeps Indian socialism apart from communistic socialism; the resolution says 'socialistic'.

questions.q: Indira Gandhi's remark quoted in the chapter on India's socialism is best summed up as
questions.a: India has its own brand of socialism and just nationalisation is not its type
o: India has its own brand of socialism and just nationalisation is not its type
India's socialism consists in the nationalisation of every sector of the economy
India has borrowed the socialism of the communist model without any change
India's socialism rules out nationalisation in every form
questions.e: Footnote 6 (p.91): 'We have always said that we have our own brand of socialism. We will nationalise the sectors where we feel the necessity. Just nationalisation is not our type of socialism'.
w: She said sectors will be nationalised where the necessity is felt, but that just nationalisation is not the type.
She spoke of 'our own brand of socialism', the opposite of borrowing a model.
She said India will nationalise sectors where the necessity is felt, so nationalisation is not ruled out.

questions.q: Which one of the following sequences places in the correct order of time the Avadi resolution of the Congress, the addition of the word 'socialist' to the Preamble, and the new Economic Policy of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
questions.a: Avadi resolution, addition of 'socialist', new Economic Policy
o: Avadi resolution, addition of 'socialist', new Economic Policy
Addition of 'socialist', Avadi resolution, new Economic Policy
Avadi resolution, new Economic Policy, addition of 'socialist'
New Economic Policy, Avadi resolution, addition of 'socialist'
questions.e: p.86: Avadi session 1955; 42nd Amendment 1976 added 'socialist'; the new Economic Policy (1991) diluted the socialist credentials.
w: The chapter says the Congress resolved on a socialistic pattern as early as 1955, before the 1976 addition.
The new Economic Policy (1991) came after the 1976 amendment, which it is said to have diluted.
The Economic Policy of 1991 is the latest of the three; Avadi (1955) is the earliest.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of democratic socialism as described in the chapter?
questions.a: Nationalisation of all means of production and distribution
o: Nationalisation of all means of production and distribution
Faith in a mixed economy in which the public and private sectors co-exist
The aim of ending poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity
In the Indian version, a blend of Marxism and Gandhism
questions.e: p.86: nationalisation of all means of production and distribution, with abolition of private property, belongs to communistic (state) socialism, not democratic socialism.
w: The chapter says democratic socialism holds faith in a mixed economy; this is a feature.
The Supreme Court quote gives this as the aim of democratic socialism; this is a feature.
The Supreme Court describes Indian socialism as this blend; this is a feature of the Indian brand.

questions.q:
With reference to the Congress resolution at the Avadi session, as quoted in the chapter, consider the following statements:

1. The resolution speaks of furthering the objectives stated in the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy.
2. The resolution speaks of an equitable distribution of the national wealth.
3. The resolution provides for the private ownership of all the principal means of production.
4. The resolution speaks of production being progressively speeded up.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 5, p.91. Statement 2 is correct: fn 5, p.91. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 5, p.91: the principal means of production are to be under social ownership or control. Statement 4 is correct: fn 5, p.91.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the order of events mentioned in the chapter on socialism:

1. The Nakara judgment (1982) preceded the new Economic Policy of 1991.
2. The Pant University judgment (2000) preceded the new Economic Policy of 1991.
3. The Nakara judgment (1982) preceded the addition of the word 'socialist' to the Preamble.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86, fn 8: 1982 is earlier than 1991. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 7, p.91: 2000 is later than 1991. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.86, fn 8: 1982 is later than 1976.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.86
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the types of socialism contrasted in the chapter:

1. Communistic socialism is also known as state socialism.
2. Democratic socialism holds faith in a mixed economy.
3. Democratic socialism involves the abolition of private property.
4. State socialism holds that the public and private sectors should co-exist side by side.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.86: that marks communistic socialism. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.86: that is democratic socialism.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The aims of democratic socialism cited in the chapter come from the G.B. Pant University case (2000).
2. The blend of Marxism and Gandhism is cited from the Nakara case (1982).
3. The Kesavananda Bharati case is cited for the view that Indian socialism leans towards Gandhism.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 7, p.91. Statement 2 is correct: fn 8, p.91. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 8, p.91: that observation is from Nakara, not Kesavananda Bharati.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the new Economic Policy of 1991:

1. It was adopted before the Nakara judgment of 1982.
2. According to the chapter, it has diluted the socialist credentials of the Indian State.
3. It was followed by an amendment deleting the word 'socialist' from the Preamble.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.86, fn 8: 1991 is later than 1982. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.91: the Preamble has been amended only once, in 1976.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.86
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Avadi resolution speaks of an equitable distribution of the national wealth.
2. Indira Gandhi said that India will nationalise the sectors where the necessity is felt.
3. The Supreme Court has described Indian socialism as a blend of Marxism and Gandhism.
4. The Indian brand of socialism is a democratic socialism and not a communistic socialism.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 5, p.91. Statement 2 is correct: fn 6, p.91. Statement 3 is correct: p.86. Statement 4 is correct: p.86.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.91
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Certain Directive Principles carried socialist content before the word 'socialist' was added to the Preamble.
2. The addition made explicit what was hitherto implicit in the Constitution.
3. The Avadi resolution was adopted after the word 'socialist' was added.
4. The word 'socialist' was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.86: Avadi was 1955, before 1976. Statement 4 is correct: p.86.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indira Gandhi's remark quoted in the chapter:

1. She said that India's socialism is the same as that of the communist States.
2. She said that India will nationalise the sectors where the necessity is felt.
3. She said that just nationalisation is not India's type of socialism.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 6, p.91: she spoke of India's own brand of socialism. Statement 2 is correct: fn 6, p.91. Statement 3 is correct: fn 6, p.91.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Congress adopted its resolution on a socialistic pattern of society at Avadi in 1955.
2. That resolution speaks of the principal means of production being under social ownership or control.
3. That resolution speaks of abolishing private property in all forms.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86. Statement 2 is correct: fn 5, p.91. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 5, p.91: it speaks of social ownership or control, not abolition of private property.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Nakara case was decided in 1982.
2. The G.B. Pant University case was decided in 2000.
3. The Avadi session of the Congress was held in 1955.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.91, fn 8. Statement 2 is correct: p.91, fn 7. Statement 3 is correct: p.86. So all three are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'Only two' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only two.
'None' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not none.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. State socialism holds faith in a mixed economy.
2. Democratic socialism involves the nationalisation of all means of production.
3. Indian socialism leans heavily towards Gandhian socialism.
4. The Nakara case was decided in 2000.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.86: that is democratic socialism. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.86. Statement 3 is correct: p.86. Statement 4 is incorrect: fn 8, p.91: 1982. So only one is correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not only two.
'Only three' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not only three.
'All four' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Supreme Court has said democratic socialism aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity.

How many of the statements given above are correct?

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.86, Avadi 1955. Statement-II is correct: p.86. The 1976 date shows Avadi came earlier but does not explain why the resolution was adopted.

Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Indian socialism is not a communistic socialism, which is also known as state socialism.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

w: Rejected: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I, so 'explains' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the item in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I
A. Avadi resolution of the Congress party
B. Indira Gandhi's remark

questions.e: p.86 and footnotes 5-6 (p.91).

concepts.name: Secularism in detail: types of state and definitions

questions.q: According to the chapter, the definition 'The State does not owe loyalty to any particular religion as such: it is not irreligious or anti-religious; it gives equal freedom to all religions' was given by
questions.a: P.B. Gajendragadkar, a former Chief Justice of India
o: P.B. Gajendragadkar, a former Chief Justice of India
H.R. Gokhale, the then Union Law Minister
N.A. Palkhivala, an eminent jurist and constitutional expert
M. Hidayatullah, a former Chief Justice of India
questions.e: Footnote 10 (p.92): Gokhale and Gajendragadkar are the two definers; the quoted words are Gajendragadkar's.
w: Gokhale's definition speaks of treating every religion equally and having no foundation of religion.
Palkhivala is cited for calling the Preamble the 'identity card' of the Constitution.
Hidayatullah is cited for comparing the Preamble with the American Declaration of Independence.

questions.q: A State treats religion as an enemy: it condemns every religion. In the chapter's classification of States by their attitude towards religion, it is
o: a State embodying the positive concept of secularism
questions.e: Footnote 9 (p.91): the atheistic State is anti-religion and hence condemns all religions.
w: A theocratic State is pro-religion and declares one religion as the State religion.
A secular State is neutral in religion and does not condemn any religion.
The positive concept gives all religions the same status and support from the State.

questions.q: A State declares one particular religion to be the State religion while permitting citizens to follow other faiths. In the chapter's classification of States by their attitude towards religion, it is
o: a secular State, since it permits other faiths
a State embodying the positive concept of secularism
questions.e: Footnote 9 (p.92): a theocratic State is pro-religion and declares one particular religion as the State religion.
w: The chapter's secular State does not uphold any particular religion as the State religion.
An atheistic State is anti-religion and condemns all religions.
The positive concept gives all religions the same status; a State religion contradicts it.

questions.q: Which one of the following descriptions of H.R. Gokhale's view of the secular State, quoted in the chapter, is NOT correct?
questions.a: The State will take the religion of the majority as its foundation
o: The State will take the religion of the majority as its foundation
There will be freedom and liberty of faith and worship, whatever religion one belongs to
The State will treat every religion equally
The State will not have any foundation of religion
questions.e: Footnote 10 (p.92): the State treats every religion equally 'but the State will not have any foundation of religion'. A majority-religion foundation is the opposite.
w: This is the first sentence of the quoted definition; it is correct.
The quotation says the State has nothing to do with religion except to treat every religion equally; it is correct.
The quotation ends by saying the State will not have any foundation of religion; it is correct.

questions.q: According to the chapter, the positive concept of secularism embodied in the Indian Constitution means that
questions.a: all religions, irrespective of their strength, have the same status and support from the State
o: all religions, irrespective of their strength, have the same status and support from the State
religions are supported in proportion to the number of their followers
the State keeps away from every religion and supports none
the State supports the majority religion and tolerates the others
questions.e: p.86: the Indian Constitution embodies the positive concept of secularism: all religions in the country (irrespective of their strength) have the same status and support from the State.
w: The chapter says 'irrespective of their strength'; proportion to followers contradicts it.
The positive concept includes support from the State, not abstention.
Same status for all is the rule; a favoured majority religion contradicts it.

questions.q:
With reference to the examples given in the chapter's classification of States by their attitude towards religion, consider the following statements:

1. The USA and India are both cited as examples of a secular State.
2. Pakistan and Sri Lanka are both cited as examples of a theocratic State.
3. Bangladesh and the USA are cited as examples of the same type of State.
4. Burma is cited as an example of a theocratic State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 2 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 9, p.92: Bangladesh is a theocratic example, the USA a secular one. Statement 4 is correct: fn 9, p.92.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the two definitions of secularism quoted in the chapter:

1. H.R. Gokhale said that the State is not irreligious or anti-religious.
2. P.B. Gajendragadkar said that the State does not owe loyalty to any particular religion as such.
3. H.R. Gokhale said that the State will treat every religion equally.
4. P.B. Gajendragadkar said that the State gives equal freedom to all religions.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 10, p.92: those words are Gajendragadkar's. Statement 2 is correct: fn 10, p.92. Statement 3 is correct: fn 10, p.92. Statement 4 is correct: fn 10, p.92.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's observation of 1974 on a secular State:

1. The Court made the observation before the word 'secular' was added to the Preamble.
2. The Court found a pointer to the makers' intention in the inclusion of Articles 25 to 28.
3. The Court said that the words 'secular state' were expressly mentioned in the Constitution as adopted.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.86: 1974 is earlier than 1976. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.86: the words were not expressly mentioned.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the positive concept of secularism in the Indian Constitution:

1. It means that the State supports only the religion followed by most of its citizens.
2. All religions in the country have the same status.
3. The State extends support to all religions in the country.
4. A religion's status depends on the strength of its followers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.86: all religions have the same status and support. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is correct: p.86. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.86: the status is the same irrespective of strength.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.86
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.86
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.86

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. An atheistic State declares one particular religion as the State religion.
2. A theocratic State is neutral in the matter of religion.
3. A secular State does not uphold any particular religion as the State religion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 9: that is the theocratic State; the atheistic State is anti-religion. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 9, p.92: a theocratic State is pro-religion. Statement 3 is correct: fn 9, p.92.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The classification of States by attitude towards religion has three types: atheistic, theocratic and secular.
2. Articles 25 to 28 guarantee the fundamental right to freedom of religion.
3. Pakistan is cited as an example of a theocratic State.
4. Under the positive concept, all religions, irrespective of their strength, have the same status and support from the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 9, pp.91-92. Statement 2 is correct: p.86. Statement 3 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 4 is correct: p.86.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.91
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A State that gives equal freedom to all religions without being irreligious or anti-religious fits P.B. Gajendragadkar's description.
2. A State that treats every religion equally but has no religion of its own is classed as an atheistic State.
3. A State that condemns all religions would be classed as an atheistic State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 10, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 9, p.92: that is the secular State; the atheistic State is anti-religion. Statement 3 is correct: fn 9, p.91.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the definition of the secular State given by H.R. Gokhale, as quoted in the chapter:

1. He spoke of freedom and liberty of faith and worship, whatever religion one belongs to.
2. He said that the State would have nothing to do with any religion at all, not even to treat every religion equally.
3. He said that the State would not have any foundation of religion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 10, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 10, p.92: the State has nothing to do with religion 'excepting to treat every religion equally'. Statement 3 is correct: fn 10, p.92.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The chapter's classification of States is based on the attitude of the State towards religion.
2. The classification is cited from G.S. Pande, Constitutional Law of India.
3. The classification is cited from M. Hidayatullah, Democracy in India and the Judicial Process.
4. The classification is cited from the Kesavananda Bharati judgment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 9, p.91. Statement 2 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 15, p.92: Hidayatullah's book is cited for his remark on the Preamble. Statement 4 is incorrect: fn 9 cites Pande, not a judgment.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
According to the chapter, consider the following statements:

1. Burma and Pakistan are both cited as examples of a theocratic State.
2. The USA is cited as an example of an atheistic State.
3. According to Gajendragadkar, the State is not irreligious or anti-religious.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 9, p.92: secular. Statement 3 is correct: fn 10, p.92. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not none.
'Only one' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'All three' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not all three.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A theocratic State is pro-religion and declares one particular religion as the State religion.
2. Sri Lanka is cited in the chapter as an example of a theocratic State.
3. A secular State upholds one particular religion as the State religion.
4. Under the positive concept, the State supports only the religion of the majority.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 2 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 9, p.92: a secular State upholds none. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.86: all religions have the same status and support. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' ignores statements 1 and 2.
'Only one' misses one correct statement.
'Only three' counts statement 3 or 4, which are incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. H. R. Gokhale said that the State will not have any foundation of religion.
2. In a secular State the State is neutral in the matter of religion.
3. An atheistic State is neutral in the matter of religion.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 10, p.92. Statement 2 is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 9, p.91: the atheistic State is anti-religion. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' ignores statements 1 and 2.
'Only one' misses one correct statement.
'All three' counts statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: India is a secular State although the word 'secular' appeared in the Preamble only through the 42nd Amendment of 1976.
Statement-II: In 1974 the Supreme Court said that the Constitution-makers wanted to establish a secular State, as shown by the inclusion of Articles 25 to 28.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.86. Statement-II is correct: p.86. The Court's inference of the makers' intention is the reason a secular State existed before the word was added.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I, so 'explains' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Burma is cited in the chapter as an example of a theocratic State.
Statement-II: The USA is cited in the chapter as an example of a secular State.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: fn 9, p.92. Statement-II is correct: fn 9, p.92. The two examples belong to different types; neither is the reason for the other.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I, so 'does not explain' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the item in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I
A. H.R. Gokhale
B. P.B. Gajendragadkar
C. The Supreme Court in 1974
D. A theocratic State

List-II
1. The State is not irreligious or anti-religious
2. The Constitution-makers wanted a secular State, as shown by Articles 25 to 28
3. Declares one particular religion as the State religion
4. The State will not have any foundation of religion
questions.e: p.86 and footnotes 9-10 (pp.91-92).
w: A and B are interchanged: 'no foundation of religion' is Gokhale's, 'not irreligious' is Gajendragadkar's.
C and D are interchanged: the Court's 1974 remark concerns the makers' intention, a theocratic State has a State religion.
A and C are interchanged: 'no foundation of religion' is Gokhale's, and the 1974 remark is about the makers' intention.

concepts.name: Democracy in detail: Greek origin, devices and Ambedkar's warning

questions.q: The term 'democracy' is derived from two Greek words, demos and kratia, which mean respectively
questions.e: Footnote 11 (p.92): Demos and Kratia mean 'People' and 'rule' respectively.
w: The meanings are reversed in this option: demos is 'people' and kratia is 'rule'.
Neither Greek word means law or power in the chapter's footnote.
Neither Greek word means state or order in the chapter's footnote.

questions.q: Citizens of a State collect support for a particular bill and place it before the legislature for enactment. Which device of direct democracy, as defined in the chapter, does this illustrate?
questions.e: Footnote 12 (p.92): initiative is the method by which the people can propose a bill to the legislature for enactment.
w: A referendum refers proposed legislation to the electorate for settlement by direct vote; here the people propose the bill.
A recall is the removal of a representative or officer before the end of his term.
A plebiscite obtains the opinion of the people on an issue, generally a territorial dispute.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT stated in the passage of Dr B.R. Ambedkar's concluding speech quoted in the chapter?
questions.a: Liberty, equality and fraternity are best treated as separate items
o: Liberty, equality and fraternity are best treated as separate items
Without equality, liberty would produce the supremacy of the few over the many
Equality without liberty would kill individual initiative
Political democracy cannot last unless social democracy lies at its base
questions.e: p.87: Ambedkar said the principles 'are not to be treated as separate items in a trinity'; to divorce one from the other is to defeat the purpose of democracy.
w: The passage says exactly this about liberty without equality.
The passage says exactly this about equality without liberty.
The passage opens with exactly this sentence.

questions.q: In 1997 the Supreme Court observed that the Constitution envisions an egalitarian social order giving every citizen social, economic and political justice in a social and economic democracy of the
questions.e: p.87: the Court's 1997 observation ends with 'the Bharat Republic'.
w: 'Indian Union' does not appear in the 1997 observation quoted in the chapter.
The observation names the Bharat Republic, not a 'Federal Republic'.
The observation names the Bharat Republic; the Preamble's adjectives are not part of its wording.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT listed in the chapter among the four devices of direct democracy?
questions.e: p.87: the four devices are referendum, initiative, recall and plebiscite.
w: Referendum is one of the four devices.
Initiative is one of the four devices.
Plebiscite is one of the four devices; the fourth is recall.

questions.q:
Consider the following situations and the devices of direct democracy they illustrate, according to the chapter:

1. A proposed law is referred to the voters for settlement by their direct votes: a referendum.
2. Citizens propose a bill to the legislature for enactment: a recall.
3. Voters remove an officer before the expiry of his term for failing to discharge his duties: a recall.
4. The opinion of the people of a disputed territory is obtained on its future: a plebiscite.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 12, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: fn 12, p.92: that is an initiative. Statement 3 is correct: fn 12, p.92: recall covers a representative or an officer. Statement 4 is correct: fn 12, p.92.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.92
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Dr Ambedkar's concluding speech in the Constituent Assembly, as quoted in the chapter:

1. It was delivered on 25 November 1949.
2. He said that without equality, liberty would produce the supremacy of the few over the many.
3. He said that equality without liberty would produce the supremacy of the few over the many.
4. He said that liberty can be divorced from equality without defeating the purpose of democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is correct: p.87. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.87: equality without liberty would kill individual initiative; the supremacy of the few comes from liberty without equality. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.87: to divorce one from the other is to defeat the very purpose of democracy.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.87
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about democracy in India as described in the chapter:

1. Indirect democracy is of two kinds, parliamentary and presidential.
2. The Indian Constitution provides for a presidential form of representative democracy.
3. Independence of the judiciary is among the manifestations of the democratic character of the Indian polity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.87: it provides for representative parliamentary democracy. Statement 3 is correct: p.87.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Demos means rule and kratia means people.
2. Popular sovereignty is the possession of supreme power by the people.
3. In direct democracy the people exercise their supreme power directly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: fn 11, p.92: demos is people and kratia is rule. Statement 2 is correct: p.87. Statement 3 is correct: p.87.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.92
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

2. Ambedkar delivered his concluding speech in the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949.
3. Initiative is the method by which the people can propose a bill to the legislature for enactment.
4. Democracy is of two types, direct and indirect.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is correct: p.87. Statement 3 is correct: fn 12, p.92. Statement 4 is correct: p.87.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.87
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.87
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the democratic character of the Indian polity, as described in the chapter:

1. Absence of discrimination on certain grounds is among its manifestations.
2. Universal adult franchise is listed as a manifestation, but periodic elections are not.
3. Independence of the judiciary is listed as a manifestation, but rule of law is not.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.87: universal adult franchise and periodic elections are both listed. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.87: rule of law and independence of the judiciary are both listed.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.87
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about direct democracy:

1. Switzerland is cited as an example of a State in which the people exercise their supreme power directly.
2. There are four devices of direct democracy: referendum, initiative, recall and plebiscite.
3. The Indian Constitution adopts these four devices as its main mode of democracy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is correct: p.87. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.87: it provides for representative parliamentary democracy. Statement 4 is correct: p.87.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.87
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.87
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. A referendum involves a vote of the electorate on a proposed legislation.
2. An initiative is a method by which the people propose a bill to the legislature.
3. A plebiscite is a method of removing a representative before the expiry of his term.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 12, p.92. Statement 2 is correct: fn 12, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: fn 12, p.92: that is a recall.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.92
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the types of democracy:

1. Democracy is of two types: direct and indirect.
2. In indirect democracy the supreme power is exercised through referendum, initiative, recall and plebiscite.
3. In indirect democracy the representatives elected by the people carry on the government and make the laws.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.87: these are the four devices of direct democracy. Statement 3 is correct: p.87.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.87
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

2. The term 'democratic' in the Preamble embraces social and economic democracy as well as political democracy.
3. The Indian executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies but not for its actions.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.87. Statement 2 is correct: p.87. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.87: for all its policies and actions. So only two are correct.

'Only one' misses one correct statement.
'All three' counts statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 11, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.87: two types. Statement 3 is correct: p.87. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.87: 25 November 1949. So only two are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not only one.

questions.q:

How many of the statements given above are correct?

w: 'Only one' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'Only two' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only two.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-II: Dr Ambedkar's passage quoted in the chapter is from his concluding speech in the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:

o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

List-I

B. Initiative

questions.e: Footnote 12 (p.92).

A and C are interchanged: referendum concerns legislation, recall concerns removal.

concepts.name: Tributes to the Preamble and its expert descriptions

questions.q: Which member of the Constituent Assembly, who played a significant role in making the Constitution, said of the Preamble: 'it expresses what we had thought or dreamt so long'?
questions.e: p.89: the quotation is attributed to Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer.
w: Munshi is quoted for the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'.
Bhargava is quoted for the 'soul', 'key' and 'jewel set in the Constitution'.
Hidayatullah is quoted for a different remark, that the Preamble is more than a declaration.

questions.q: Sir Ernest Barker quoted the Preamble at the opening of his popular book, which is
questions.a: Principles of Social and Political Theory (1951)
o: Principles of Social and Political Theory (1951)
Democracy in India and the Judicial Process
The Framing of India's Constitution: Select Documents
questions.e: p.90: Barker quoted the Preamble at the opening of Principles of Social and Political Theory (1951).
w: That book is by M. Hidayatullah, cited for his remark on the Preamble (fn 15).
That book is by B. Shiva Rao, cited for Ambedkar's speech (fn 12a).
That book is by G.S. Pande, cited for the classification of States (fn 9).

questions.q: Which one of the following persons described the Preamble as something that 'lays down the pattern of our political society'?
questions.e: p.90 and fn 15 (p.92): Hidayatullah said the Preamble is the soul of the Constitution which lays down the pattern of our political society.
w: Munshi's phrase was 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'.
Palkhivala's phrase was 'identity card of the Constitution'.
Barker's phrase was 'key-note' to the Constitution.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of person and description of the Preamble is NOT correct?
questions.a: N.A. Palkhivala - the 'soul' of the Constitution
o: N.A. Palkhivala - the 'soul' of the Constitution
Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer - what 'we had thought or dreamt so long'
K.M. Munshi - the 'horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic'
Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava - 'a jewel set in the Constitution'
questions.e: p.85: Palkhivala called the Preamble the 'identity card' of the Constitution; 'soul' is the word of Bhargava and Hidayatullah.
w: This pair is correct (p.89).
This pair is correct (p.89).
This pair is correct (p.89).

questions.q: Sir Ernest Barker, who called the Preamble the 'key-note' to the Constitution, is described in the chapter as
o: a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly
a former Chief Justice of India
an eminent jurist and constitutional expert of India
questions.e: p.90: Barker is described as a distinguished English political scientist.
w: That description fits K.M. Munshi.
That description fits M. Hidayatullah.
That description fits N.A. Palkhivala.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the persons quoted in the chapter on the Preamble:

1. N.A. Palkhivala is described as an eminent jurist and constitutional expert.
2. K.M. Munshi is described as a former Chief Justice of India.
3. M. Hidayatullah is described as a former Chief Justice of India.
4. Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer is described as a member of the Constituent Assembly who played a significant role in making the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.85. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.89: he is described as a member of the Drafting Committee. Statement 3 is correct: p.90. Statement 4 is correct: p.89.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.85
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.85
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.85

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the descriptions of the Preamble that use the word 'key':

1. Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava said that the Preamble is a key to the Constitution.
2. Sir Ernest Barker described the Preamble as the 'key-note' to the Constitution.
3. The Supreme Court in the Berubari Union case called the Preamble a key to the minds of the makers of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: p.90.
w: '1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.89
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sir Ernest Barker and the Preamble:

1. He described the Preamble as the 'key-note' to the Constitution.
2. He said that the Preamble states in a brief and pithy form the argument of much of his book.
3. He quoted the Preamble at the close of his book.
4. He was so moved by the text of the Preamble that he quoted it at the opening of his book.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is correct: fn 13, p.92. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.90: at the opening. Statement 4 is correct: p.90.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.90
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about M. Hidayatullah's observation on the Preamble:

1. He said that the Preamble contains a solemn resolve which nothing but an amendment under Article 368 can alter.
2. He said that the Preamble lays down the pattern of our political society.
3. He said that the Preamble is the soul of our Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.90: nothing but a revolution can alter it. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: p.90.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava's description of the Preamble:

1. He said that it expresses what the makers had thought or dreamt so long.
2. He called it the soul of the Constitution.
3. He called it a jewel set in the Constitution.
4. He called it a proper yardstick with which one can measure the worth of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.89: that is Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer's remark. Statement 2 is correct: p.89. Statement 3 is correct: p.89. Statement 4 is correct: p.89.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.89
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.89
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer and Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava:

1. Iyer said that the Preamble expresses what we had thought or dreamt so long.
2. Iyer is described as a former Chief Justice of India.
3. Bhargava is described as a member of the Constituent Assembly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.89: he is described as a member of the Constituent Assembly who played a significant role in making the Constitution. Statement 3 is correct: p.89.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.89
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.89
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava described the Preamble as a proper yardstick with which one can measure the worth of the Constitution.
2. Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer called the Preamble a key to the minds of the makers.
3. N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the soul of the Constitution.
4. Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava called the Preamble the most precious part of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.89: Iyer said it expresses what the makers had thought or dreamt so long; the phrase 'key to the minds of the makers' is the Court's in Berubari. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.85: he called it the identity card of the Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: p.89.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.89
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about K.M. Munshi as quoted in the chapter:

1. He was a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
2. He said that the phrase 'dignity of the individual' signifies only material betterment.
3. His 'horoscope' description referred to the 'sovereign socialist secular democratic republic'.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.89: he said the Constitution also recognises that the personality of every individual is sacred. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.89: he said 'our sovereign democratic republic'.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.89
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the books cited in the footnotes on the Preamble:

1. Hidayatullah's remark on the Preamble is cited from his book Democracy in India and the Judicial Process.
2. Barker's quotation of the Preamble is from Democracy in India and the Judicial Process.
3. Barker's book Principles of Social and Political Theory was published in 1951.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 15, p.92. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.90: Barker quoted it in Principles of Social and Political Theory. Statement 3 is correct: p.90.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.92
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava called the Preamble the soul of the Constitution.
2. Sir Ernest Barker called the Preamble the horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic.
3. Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer was a member of the Constituent Assembly.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.89: that is Munshi. Statement 3 is correct: p.89. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not none.
'Only one' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
