questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. K.M. Munshi explained the phrase 'dignity of the individual'.
2. Munshi said the personality of every individual is sacred.
3. Munshi called the Preamble the soul of the Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.89. Statement 2 is correct: p.89. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.89: the soul is Bhargava's (and Hidayatullah's) word; Munshi said horoscope. So only two are correct.
w: 'Only one' misses one correct statement.
'Only three' counts statement 3, which is incorrect.
'All three' counts statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Sir Ernest Barker is described as a distinguished English political scientist.
2. M. Hidayatullah is described as a former Chief Justice of India.
3. N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the identity card of the Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: p.85. So all three are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'Only two' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only two.
'None' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not none.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Sir Ernest Barker quoted the Preamble at the opening of his book Principles of Social and Political Theory.
Statement-II: Barker wrote that he was all the more moved to quote it because he was proud that the people of India should begin their independent life by subscribing to a political tradition that the west calls western.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.90. Statement-II is correct: fn 14, p.92: he gives this as his reason for quoting it. Footnote 14 gives Barker's own reason for quoting the Preamble.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I, so 'explains' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: M. Hidayatullah said that the Preamble resembles the American Declaration of Independence but is more than a declaration.
Statement-II: Hidayatullah's remark is quoted at the opening of Barker's book Principles of Social and Political Theory.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.90. Statement-II is incorrect: p.90 and fn 15, p.92: Barker quoted the Preamble itself there; Hidayatullah's remark is from his Democracy in India and the Judicial Process.
w: Rejected: it treats both statements as correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: it treats both statements as correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the person in List-I with the description of the Preamble in List-II.

List-I
A. N.A. Palkhivala
B. K.M. Munshi
C. Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava
D. Sir Ernest Barker

List-II
1. The horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic
2. The key-note to the Constitution
3. A proper yardstick with which one can measure the worth of the Constitution
4. The identity card of the Constitution
w: A and B are interchanged: identity card is Palkhivala's, horoscope is Munshi's.
C and D are interchanged: the yardstick is Bhargava's, the key-note Barker's.
A and D are interchanged: identity card is Palkhivala's, key-note Barker's.

concepts.name: The Berubari, Kesavananda Bharati and LIC cases on the Preamble

questions.q: Which one of the following arranges the three cases in the chapter in order of time, earliest first, in which the Supreme Court dealt with the status of the Preamble?
questions.a: Berubari Union, Kesavananda Bharati, LIC of India
o: Berubari Union, Kesavananda Bharati, LIC of India
Kesavananda Bharati, Berubari Union, LIC of India
Berubari Union, LIC of India, Kesavananda Bharati
LIC of India, Berubari Union, Kesavananda Bharati
questions.e: pp.90-92: Berubari Union (1960), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), LIC of India (1995).
w: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) rejected the earlier Berubari opinion (1960), so it cannot come first.
LIC of India (1995) is the latest of the three, not the middle one.
LIC of India (1995) is the latest, so it cannot be first.

questions.q: A petitioner argues that the Preamble cannot be amended at all because it is not a part of the Constitution. Which decision described in the chapter first rejected the premise of this argument?
questions.e: p.90: in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Court rejected the earlier opinion and held the Preamble is a part; LIC of India (1995) held so again.
w: Berubari Union is the opinion which held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.
LIC of India (1995) again held the Preamble integral, but after Kesavananda had already rejected the premise.
The 1976 Act amended the Preamble; it is not a judicial decision on whether the Preamble is a part.

questions.q: 'The edifice of our Constitution is based upon the basic elements mentioned in the Preamble. If any of these elements are removed, the structure will not survive.' This observation was made by the Supreme Court in
questions.a: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
LIC of India v. Consumer Education and Research Centre (1995)
G.B. Pant University v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2000)
questions.e: p.91: the observation is quoted from the Kesavananda Bharati case, where the Court said the Preamble can be amended subject to the basic features.
w: Berubari held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution and was held wrong in this regard.
LIC of India held the Preamble an integral part; the 'edifice' observation is not attributed to it.
The Pant University case is cited for the aims of democratic socialism.

questions.q: In Kesavananda Bharati, the petitioner contended that the amending power in Article 368
questions.a: cannot be used to destroy or damage the basic elements or fundamental features of the Constitution enshrined in the Preamble
o: cannot be used to destroy or damage the basic elements or fundamental features of the Constitution enshrined in the Preamble
cannot be used to amend any provision of the Constitution that is not enforceable in a court
can be used to amend the Preamble only with the consent of the Supreme Court
cannot be used to amend the Constitution after the Preamble has been enacted
questions.e: p.90: the petitioner contended that Article 368 cannot be used to destroy or damage the basic elements or fundamental features enshrined in the Preamble.
w: The contention was about basic elements in the Preamble, not about enforceability.
The chapter mentions no requirement of the Court's consent.
The Preamble was enacted last; the contention was about the basic elements, not the time of enactment.

questions.q: An amendment under Article 368 is proposed that would remove one of the basic elements mentioned in the Preamble. According to the Kesavananda Bharati holding as described in the chapter, this amendment
questions.a: cannot be made, since the Constitution would not remain the same Constitution
o: cannot be made, since the Constitution would not remain the same Constitution
can be made, since the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution
can be made, since Article 368 reaches every part of the Constitution without limit
can be made, but only if the Supreme Court gives its prior consent
questions.e: p.91: basic elements contained in the Preamble cannot be altered under Article 368; if removed, it will not be the same Constitution.
w: That was the Berubari view, which Kesavananda held wrong.
The Court held that basic elements in the Preamble cannot be altered by an amendment under Article 368.
The chapter mentions no such consent; it states a limit on the amending power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the order of the cases and the amendment concerning the Preamble:

1. The Berubari Union opinion (1960) preceded the Kesavananda Bharati judgment (1973).
2. The LIC of India judgment (1995) came after the Preamble had been amended in 1976.
3. The Kesavananda Bharati judgment came after the Preamble was amended in 1976.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: pp.90-92: 1960 and 1973. Statement 2 is correct: p.91 and p.90. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.90-91: 1973 is earlier than 1976.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legal position of the Preamble:

1. Being a part of the Constitution, the Preamble is a source of power to the legislature.
2. The Preamble is non-justiciable, that is, its provisions are not enforceable in courts of law.
3. Where the terms used in an article are ambiguous, some assistance in interpretation may be taken from the objectives in the Preamble.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.90: it is neither a source of power nor a prohibition. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: p.90, Berubari.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kesavananda Bharati case:

1. In Kesavananda Bharati the Court held that the Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers but is not a part of the Constitution.
2. The petitioner contended that the amending power cannot be used to destroy basic elements enshrined in the Preamble.
3. The Court stated that the opinion in the Berubari Union case on this point was wrong.
4. The Court held that the Preamble can be amended, subject to no amendment being done to the basic features.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.90: that was the Berubari view, which Kesavananda rejected. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: p.91. Statement 4 is correct: p.91.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the enactment of the Preamble:

1. Like any other part of the Constitution, the Preamble was enacted by the Constituent Assembly.
2. The Preamble was enacted before the rest of the Constitution so that the other provisions could conform to it.
3. The Supreme Court's present opinion that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution is in consonance with the opinion of the founding fathers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.90: it was enacted after the rest, to ensure its conformity with the Constitution as adopted. Statement 3 is correct: p.90.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the names and references in the cases:

1. The Kesavananda Bharati case is cited as Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).
2. The 1995 case is cited as LIC of India v. Consumer Education and Research Centre.
3. The Berubari reference concerned the 1958 Indo-Pakistan agreement relating to the Berubari Union and exchange of enclaves.
4. The Preamble is neither a source of power to the legislature nor a prohibition upon its powers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: fn 17, p.92. Statement 2 is correct: fn 18, p.92. Statement 3 is correct: fn 16, p.92. Statement 4 is correct: p.90.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.92
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.92
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.92

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble in the courts:

1. A law of Parliament is invalid merely because it conflicts with the Preamble, since the Preamble is a prohibition upon the legislature.
2. A court may take assistance from the Preamble when an article is ambiguous.
3. A court can enforce the provisions of the Preamble directly, since the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.90: the Preamble is neither a source of power nor a prohibition upon the powers of the legislature. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.90: the Preamble is non-justiciable; its provisions are not enforceable in courts of law.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.90
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In the LIC of India case the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
2. The LIC of India case was decided before the Kesavananda Bharati case.
3. The Berubari Union case said that the Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers of the Constitution.
4. The Berubari Union opinion held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is incorrect: pp.90, 92: 1995 is after 1973. Statement 3 is correct: p.90. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.90: the Court opined that the Preamble is not a part.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amendability of the Preamble:

1. The question whether the Preamble can be amended under Article 368 arose for the first time in Kesavananda Bharati.
2. In Kesavananda Bharati the Court held that the Preamble, though a part of the Constitution, cannot be amended at all.
3. The basic elements contained in the Preamble cannot be altered by an amendment under Article 368.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.91: it can be amended, subject to the basic features. Statement 3 is correct: p.91.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.90
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.90
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The 1976 amendment of the Preamble was held to be valid.
2. The Preamble was amended again after the LIC of India judgment of 1995.
3. The only amendment of the Preamble came before the Kesavananda Bharati judgment had held it amendable.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.91. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.91: it has been amended only once, in 1976. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.90-91: 1976 is later than 1973.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.91
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.91
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In LIC of India the Court held the Preamble to be an integral part of the Constitution.
2. In Berubari Union the Court said that the Preamble shows the general purposes behind the several provisions of the Constitution.
3. In Kesavananda Bharati the Court held that the Preamble cannot be amended at all.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.91: it can be amended, subject to the basic features. So only two are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not none.
'Only one' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'All three' miscounts: 2 statement(s) are correct, not all three.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Kesavananda Bharati case was decided in 1960.
2. The Preamble is non-justiciable.
3. In the LIC of India case the Court held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.
4. The Preamble was enacted before the rest of the Constitution.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.90 / fn 17: 1973. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.90: it held it an integral part. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.90: after. So only one is correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not only two.
'Only three' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not only three.
'All four' miscounts: 1 statement(s) are correct, not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The President of the Constituent Assembly put the question 'that Preamble stands part of the Constitution'.
2. The motion was adopted.
3. The Berubari Union opinion was given on a reference made by the President under Article 143.
4. The Preamble may be amended without any limit under Article 368.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.90. Statement 2 is correct: p.90. Statement 3 is correct: fn 16, p.92. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.91: subject to the basic features. So only three are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only one.
'Only two' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not only two.
'All four' miscounts: 3 statement(s) are correct, not all four.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Preamble is non-justiciable.
Statement-II: The Preamble is a part of the Constitution.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.90. Statement-II is correct: p.90. Being a part of the Constitution does not make its provisions enforceable; the chapter lists non-justiciability separately.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does give the reason for Statement-I, so 'does not explain' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Preamble cannot be amended so as to remove its basic elements.
Statement-II: The Court observed that if any of the basic elements mentioned in the Preamble are removed, the structure will not survive and it will not be the same Constitution.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.91. Statement-II is correct: p.91. The loss of identity of the Constitution is the reason the basic elements are protected from amendment.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not give the reason for Statement-I, so 'explains' fails.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the decision or event in List-I with its holding in List-II.

List-I
A. Berubari Union (1960)
B. Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
C. LIC of India (1995)
D. The 1976 amendment of the Preamble

List-II
1. The Preamble is held an integral part of the Constitution
2. The Preamble is a key to the minds of the makers but not a part of the Constitution
3. The amendment was held to be valid
4. The earlier opinion is rejected; the Preamble can be amended subject to the basic features
w: A and B are interchanged: Berubari said not a part, Kesavananda rejected that opinion.
C and D are interchanged: the 1995 case held it an integral part; the 1976 amendment was held valid.
A and C are interchanged: Berubari said not a part, LIC held it an integral part.
